title: Modifications and generic-fibre modifications
statement: For schemes $X,Y$ [def-pc-scheme], a morphism $f:X\to Y$ is a modification if it is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] and there exists an open $U\subset Y$ such that both $U$ and $f^{-1}(U)$ are schematically dense [def-trf-schematically-dense-open] and the restriction $f^{-1}(U)\to U$ along the open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] is an isomorphism. Given schemes $T,E$, a specified morphism $e:E\to T$ and $y:Y\to T$, call $f$ an $e$-modification if it is a modification and the canonical base-change morphism $X\times_T E\to Y\times_T E$ [def-pc-fibre-product], using $y\circ f$ as the structure map of $X$, is an isomorphism. In particular, when $E=\eta$ is the generic point of $T$, this is an $\eta$-modification. This is the actual induced map, not an assertion that the two fibre products merely admit some isomorphism.

mathlib_searches.query: A modification is proper and is an isomorphism on schematically dense opens; an eta modification is an isomorphism on the generic fibre
A modification is a proper morphism inducing an isomorphism over schematically dense opens in both source and target

mathlib_searches.results: No exact general notion or duplicate declaration. Blueprint searches strict semistable and strictly semistable: 0 hits. Schematic density occurs inline in NagataSketchClosure, not as a predicate. Orgogozo.IsModification is restricted to reduced, locally Noetherian compact targets and uses topological density. NodalFamilyEtaleLocalModel gives a universal nodal model over Z[a], not strict semistability. MultipointedCurve additionally specifies a marking. PureDimension already gives fibrewise pure dimension and is reused.
